title: On-call & Incident Response: Rotations, Runbooks, Postmortems, Game Days, Status Page + Comms Templates
author: Jordan Liu
content:
Summary:
This document consolidates Redwood Inference's on-call and incident response processes: incident severity definitions, the incident lifecycle, primary runbooks for common failure modes, postmortem templates and timelines, on-call rotation rules and escalation matrices, recommended game day exercises, and both internal and customer-facing status page / communications templates. It is intended for SREs, platform engineers, product owners, and on-call responders.

Scope and applicability:
- Applies to all production-facing Redwood services (hosted API, dedicated control plane, private deployment control plane components) and associated infra (GPU fleet, routing, databases, logging, alerting).
- Excludes non-production experimental sandboxes and personal dev workloads.

Incident severity definitions (use these to triage and route):
1) Sev 0 (Critical outage): Total service unavailability or data loss impacting >25% of paid customers or violating SLA (example: Control plane down across region, or corruption of persistent metadata). Immediate page to all-hands channel and exec-esc. Target response: 0-5 minutes.
2) Sev 1 (High): Significant degradation or partial outage impacting >5% of customers or causing severe latency/cost regressions. Target response: 5-15 minutes.
3) Sev 2 (Medium): Degraded functionality for a subset of users or non-critical latency regressions with mitigation available. Target response: 30-60 minutes.
4) Sev 3 (Low): Non-urgent issues, grooming items, or feature regressions with no immediate impact to customers. Respond during business hours.

Incident lifecycle (high-level steps):
1) Detection & alerting: Automated alerts from monitoring, or customer report via support channel.
2) Triage: On-call engineer classifies severity and assigns incident owner (IRO).
3) Mobilize & communicate: Open incident in Incident Board (Confluence incident page + PagerDuty incident). Post initial internal comms.
4) Mitigate: Apply runbooks or temporary mitigations to restore service or reduce blast radius.
5) Fix: Implement root-cause fix with change control (canary + rollback plan).
6) Recovery confirmation & closure: Verify service health meets SLOs. Close incident after stakeholder sign-off.
7) Postmortem & follow-up: Run a blameless postmortem, assign action items and due dates, link to incident and release notes.

Roles & responsibilities:
- Incident Owner (IRO): Drives incident resolution, coordinates comms, ensures runbook actions are executed.
- Secondary/Shadow: Hands-on support for troubleshooting and remediation steps.
- PagerDuty Lead: Escalates to next tier when on-call does not acknowledge.
- Engineering Manager / Product Owner: Notified for Sev 0/1; approves customer comms.
- Communications Lead (SRE or Support): Publishes status page updates and coordinates external comms.

Escalation matrix (summary):
- Triage within 5 minutes for Sev 0/1. If unacknowledged, PagerDuty escalates at 5m / 10m / 20m intervals to Tier-2 and Tier-3.
- For Sev 0, notify on-call EM and Director at 15 minutes if unresolved.
- Use Slack channel #incident-{region} for real-time coordination, and #incident-exec for exec-level updates (read-only except for designated leads).

Runbooks (quick index + canonical location):
- API Gateway: latency 95p > 1.5s -> Steps: check gateway pods, backpressure metrics, throttling rules, NATS queue depth. (See runbook below)
- Model serving workers OOMs: Steps: gather recent config, inspect kernel logs, check quantized model crate, temporarily scale down concurrency or revert recent model versions.
- Control plane DB write failures: Steps: failover read-replica, check WAL lag, alert DB-owners.
- GPU node failure: Steps: cordon node, restart inference service, re-schedule KV caches.
- Auth / Token service outage: Steps: flip to fallback auth provider, rotate short-lived tokens, communicate to integrators.

Example runbook: API Gateway high latency (title: api-gateway-high-latency)
- Trigger: Monitoring alert: gateway_request_latency_95p > 1.5s for 3m.
- PagerDuty severity: Sev 1.
- Initial checks (5m):
  1) Check PagerDuty incident and acknowledge.
  2) Open incident page template and fill Summary, StartTime, Affected Services, Initial Hypothesis.
  3) Run: kubectl -n infra get pods -l app=api-gateway && kubectl top pod for cpu/mem.
  4) Check gateway logs (last 15m): curl "https://logs.redwood-internal/api?query=gateway_error_rate" or use Kibana dashboard 'API Gateway Overview'.
- Temporary mitigations (10-30m):
  1) If pods are saturated, scale replicas: kubectl scale deployment/api-gateway --replicas=<N+2>.
  2) If backend overload suspected, enable circuit-breaker to reject noncritical routes: apply yaml patch.
  3) If new deploy within 30m, roll back to previous stable revision via: kubectl rollout undo deployment/api-gateway.
- Root cause & fix (30-180m):
  1) Capture pprof/traces, collect request samples and slow traces.
  2) Identify faulty downstream (e.g., model router) and execute downstream runbook.
  3) After fix, monitor 95p latency for 30m before closure.
- Owner & follow-up: assign follow-up ticket and add to next weekly SRE review.

Postmortem template and timeline (blameless):
- Timeline: Postmortem draft within 48 hours of incident closure. Review with stakeholders within 5 business days. Final postmortem published to Confluence within 10 business days.
- Template fields (fill each):
  - Title (string)
  - Severity (Sev0/1/2/3)
  - Start / End times (UTC)
  - Services impacted (list)
  - Detection vector (monitoring / customer report / other)
  - Contributing factors (bullet list)
  - Root cause (concise sentence)
  - Timeline (minute-level where possible)
  - Mitigation steps taken during incident
  - Corrective actions (Owner / Due date / Status)
  - Post-incident verification plan
  - Lessons learned and preventive measures
  - Links: incident ticket, runbooks used, relevant PRs and logs

On-call rotations & rules:
- Rotation cadence: 1 week primary on-call, daily secondary/backup. Primary is responsible for first response, ticket updates, and initial comms. Secondary supports escalation.
- Coverage hours: 24/7 for production regions. Weekdays and weekend coverage are identical.
- Handoff: Handover doc required at shift start with outstanding incidents, maintenance windows, scheduled rollouts. Handover must be posted in #oncall-handoffs and attached to the incident board if active.
- Time off / swaps: Use PagerDuty schedule swaps; on-call swaps require EM approval at least 48 hours before shift.
- Burnout mitigation: No more than 2 consecutive weeks on-call without manager sign-off. After a Sev 0 week, the engineer receives a rest week (optional replacement by EM).

Game days (exercise program):
- Frequency: Quarterly service-focused game days, monthly smaller tabletop exercises.
- Goals: Validate runbooks, test playbook effectiveness, ensure monitoring/alerting fidelity, rehearse customer comms.
- Example scenario: Control-plane partial outage during a model rollout. Runbook steps exercised: rollback, cache invalidation, canary rollout policy. Observability checks: request tracing, KV cache metrics.
- After action: Capture time-to-detect, time-to-mitigate, and time-to-recover metrics. Create 2 action items per game day.

Status page & customer comms templates
- Internal status page process:
  1) For Sev 1/0 incidents, open an internal status page entry and post initial summary in 15 minutes.
  2) Update every 30 minutes until mitigation, then every 60 minutes while resolving.
  3) Mark resolved only after SLO verifications and follow-up task creation.
- External / customer-facing status templates (use product marketing and legal review for Sev 0 communications when customer-sensitive data is involved):
  - Initial external:
    Title: "Incident: Service disruption affecting {region}"
    Time: {start_UTC}
    Summary: "We are currently investigating an issue affecting {service}. Some customers may experience increased latency or failed requests. Our engineers are actively working to restore service."
    Impact: "All customers in {region} / subset of customers using {feature}"
    Next update: "We will provide an update within 30 minutes."
    Contact: "support@redwood-inference.com"
  - Update external (example after mitigation):
    Title: "Update: Mitigation in place — partial restoration for {service}"
    Summary: "A mitigation has been applied to reduce impact. We are continuing work to fully restore service. A full post-incident report will be published within 10 business days."
  - Resolution external:
    Title: "Resolved: Service restored — postmortem to follow"
    Summary: "The issue has been resolved at {end_UTC}. Services have returned to normal and are being monitored. We will publish a detailed postmortem within 10 business days."

Customer comms playbook (short checklist):
1) Confirm scope and SLO impact with IRO and EM.
2) Draft initial external status message, get EM + legal sign-off for Sev 0.
3) Publish to status.redwood-inference.com and notify customers via in-console messages for Dedicated/Private customers.
4) Send targeted email to affected customers when the blast radius is well understood.
5) Publish postmortem link to status page and include customer-facing summary.

Operational tooling and checks:
- Incident board template: always include fields: Title, Start time, Severity, Affected services, Owner, Status, Mitigation steps, Next update ETA, Links.
- Automations: Slack alert -> creates PagerDuty incident -> creates Confluence incident page from template. Ensure automation maintains a ticket ID mapping.
- Monitoring SLO thresholds (examples):
  - Hosted API availability: 99.95% monthly (SLO). Alert if rolling 1h availability < 99.9%.
  - 95p latency for text generation < 350ms (regional) — alert on rolling 15m breaches.
  - Error rate > 0.5% rolling 10m for production endpoints -> warn; > 1% -> Sev 1.

Post-incident actions & tracking:
- Each postmortem must create corrective action tickets in the SRE board tagged with incident ID and due dates.
- Owners must update ticket status weekly until resolved.
- Quarterly reliability review: Present top 5 incidents and long-lived action items.

Appendix: templates and snippets
- Incident page starter (copy into new incident page):
  ---
  Title: {Short description}
  Start time (UTC): {YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM}
  Severity: {Sev0/1/2/3}
  Owner: {name/email}
  Affected services: {list}
  Initial hypothesis: {one line}
  Initial mitigation attempted: {list}
  Next update ETA: {minutes}
  Links: {PagerDuty, Logs, Dashboards}
  ---

- PagerDuty escalation CLI examples:
  pd incidents create --service "api-gateway" --title "High latency" --urgency high

- Status page external message (short JSON for status service):
  {
    "status":"investigating",
    "components":[{"name":"Hosted API","status":"degraded"}],
    "body":"We are currently investigating reports of increased latency for text-generation requests in {region}.",
    "update_interval":30
  }
  (Note: replace placeholders, and ensure EM sign-off for sev0 messages.)

- Postmortem checklist (before publishing):
  1) Technical timeline reviewed and validated by responders.
  2) Action items created and owners assigned.
  3) Customer-facing summary approved.
  4) Relevant runbooks updated with lessons learned.

Frequently asked questions (FAQ):
- Q: When should I call a Sev 0?
  A: If the outage impacts broad customer access, causes data loss, or violates SLA, escalate to Sev 0 immediately. When in doubt, err on the side of higher severity and consult your EM.
- Q: Who writes the postmortem?
  A: The Incident Owner drafts the postmortem; reviewers include on-call secondary, EM, and product owner.
- Q: How are customers notified for Dedicated/Private deployments?
  A: Use the in-console broadcast for Dedicated customers and coordinate with the account team for Private customers.

Ownership and governance:
- Document owner: SRE playbooks lead (owner: eng-sre).
- Review cadence: Annual review or after any Sev 0/1 event.
- Exceptions: Any deviation from this playbook during an incident must be recorded in the incident timeline and justified in the postmortem.

Contact & escalation directory (short):
- SRE PagerDuty: SRE-Team-Oncall (pagerduty ID: pd-sre-01)
- Platform EM: em-platform@redwood-inference.com
- Support (external-facing): support@redwood-inference.com
- Security incident response: sec-incident@redwood-inference.com
